page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. This server features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB per core, alongside 118 GB of local storage. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling due to the single physical core constraint. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average, whereas the multi-core CPU performance falls into the lower percentile. Memory bandwidth tests show weak throughput, with read-only large block transfers at 25.26 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.86 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, demonstrate average execution speeds, while database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the lower performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ds_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and local storage, though it presents a tradeoff in multi-threaded processing and memory-intensive operations. The inclusion of 118 GB of local storage provides value for temporary data caching. This server is suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, development environments, and single-threaded utility tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or extensive multi-core parallelization.
